title: Non-Thermal Technologies — Microfiltration, Ultrafiltration, Reverse Osmosis, HPP, Ultra-High-Voltage Electric Fields and Cold Plasma
shortDescription: Membrane separation and emerging non-thermal processes: principles, parameters and applications.
genZNote: Non-thermal = treat the food without cooking it. Gentle on flavour, ruthless on microbes. Pore size order is MF > UF > NF > RO.

sections.heading: Membrane Processes
sections.body: RO requires pressure higher than the osmotic pressure (typically tens of bars); fouling and concentration polarisation affect flux; CIP is essential.

Whey protein concentrate, milk protein concentrates, juice clarification, cheese yield
Almost all solutes; only water passes

sections.heading: High Pressure Processing, PEF/Ultra-High-Voltage Fields and Cold Plasma
bullets: HPP (hydrostatic pressure): 300–600 MPa for minutes, isostatic and quasi-instantaneous throughout the food; inactivates vegetative cells, yeasts, moulds, viruses; spores are resistant unless combined with heat; used for juices, guacamole, ready meals, meat; packs must be flexible.

Pulsed electric fields / ultra-high-voltage electric fields: short high-voltage pulses (kV/cm) cause electroporation of microbial membranes; suitable for pumpable liquids (juices, milk); non-thermal at low temperature.

Cold plasma: ionised gas (reactive oxygen/nitrogen species, UV photons, charged particles) at near-ambient temperature; surface decontamination of fresh produce, grains, packaging; research/commercial emerging; effects on lipid oxidation and regulation still being studied.
Common advantages: fresh-like flavour, nutrients retained; limits: cost, validation, not for all foods, regulatory approval as novel processes.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Non-thermal technologies such as membrane separation, high pressure, pulsed electric fields and cold plasma inactivate microbes or separate components with minimal heat.
keyFacts: MF removes bacteria; UF concentrates proteins.

commonTraps: Do not say HPP kills bacterial spores easily.
mustRemember: Pore size: MF > UF > NF > RO.
